conviction_note: Near-balanced: the consensus bar for Networks (+6% QoQ sales, ~49.7% Networks adj GM) sits well above the guide's wording ('above +1%', 48-50%) while memory costs kept rising and Danske flags US capex deferrals into 2027 for the Q4 guide; against that, a SEK 5bn inventory build for Q3 deliveries, India deliveries slipping from Q2 into Q3, possible IPR catch-up from July licences, an active SEK 15bn buyback and a stock 5% off its 52-week low with 10 days to cover on the ADR short. Findings sum -0.4; scaled number is (2*0.48-1)*9 = -0.36. The two agree in sign and roughly in size; abs_move is set on the name's real print reactions (Q3'25 ~+20%, Q1'26 -5.4%, Q2'26 -7% to -10% intraday) and the 8.4% event-implied move, not on the 6-K noise in the baseline.
bar: Infront consensus compiled 2026-10-08 from 16 analysts: net sales SEK 55.4bn, Networks SEK 35.1bn, CSS SEK 15.2bn, Enterprise SEK 4.7bn, adj gross margin 47.3%, adj EBITA SEK 7.9bn (14.2%) (https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/, 2026-10-12). Ericsson's own data-points page (2026-09-11) independently states Networks consensus +6% QoQ against its guide 'above the 3-year seasonal +1%' and CSS consensus +3% (https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points). Networks adj GM guide 48-50%; analyst average at guide time 49.7% (https://www.placera.se/telegram/ericsson-spar-just-bruttomarg-networks-48-50-3-kv-est-49-7-20260714). Two agreeing sources on the Networks bar, so sizes are not capped. Q2 Networks sales were SEK 33.0bn (Light Reading), so 35.1bn is +6.4% QoQ.
positioning_check: ADR short interest 74,777,498 shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, ~2.3% of 3.25bn shares outstanding, 10.21 days to cover against ADR volume (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/eric/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 by the sweep). Days to cover is high but measured against the thin ADR line; part of it is likely Stockholm-arbitrage hedging, so it is a moderate rather than crowded short on a whole-company basis. Swedish FI short register not reachable in search. Options: skew_25d is null in the baseline (not available); put/call OI ratio 0.31 (call-heavy); event-implied move 8.4%, ATM spread 22% of mid. Tape: spot $9.625, -29.95% from 52w high (SEK 128.45 on 2026-06-03), +5.19% off 52w low, 20d -4.04%, 5d +1.74%.

findings.finding: The Networks sales bar is set well above the company's own guide wording: Infront consensus (2026-10-08) has Networks at SEK 35.1bn, +6.4% QoQ on Q2's SEK 33.0bn, while Ericsson guided only 'above the 3-year seasonal +1%'; FX adds ~+2% QoQ (USD/SEK 9.61, +3% QoQ, per Ericsson's data-points page; actual rate is slightly below the 9.7 the outlook assumed), so the bar needs roughly +4% organic QoQ, about three points above the seasonal pattern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: sales SEK 52.7bn vs 53.9bn Bloomberg consensus (-2.2%) with adj EBITA a small beat; stock fell ~7% at 09:37 and as much as -10.3% intraday in Stockholm (placera 2026-07-14). Q1 2026: sales -10% YoY on North America and SEK strength; ADR -5.4% (tech-insider). Sales misses have been sold even when EBITA beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide-vs-consensus gap is printed on Ericsson's own page, so it is known; what is not priced is which way it resolves. If the market believed +6% was safe the stock would not sit 5% off its 52-week low after two consecutive negative print reactions; if it believed a miss was coming the implied move would not be a plain 8.4% with a call-heavy put/call OI of 0.31.
findings.independence: Consensus figures from Infront via https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/ (2026-10-12) agree (Networks 35.1bn). Q2 Networks SEK 33.0bn from https://www.lightreading.com/finance/ericsson-warns-of-price-rises-to-counter-high-component-costs. Shares the Ericsson data-points document with finding 2's guide range.

findings.finding: Q2 free cash flow collapsed to SEK 0.4bn because inventory rose from SEK 25.7bn to SEK 30.7bn 'ahead of planned Q3 deliveries', and Jefferies attributed Q2's ~1% sales shortfall to India delivery timing; both point to Networks volume shifting into Q3, which is what an above-seasonal guide and a +6% consensus need.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, the last print where North American volumes rebounded and earnings beat, the ADR rose ~20.6% intraday (fool.com 2025-10-14). Volume-led beats have paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the Q2 report, but the stock has kept falling since (ADR 30% off its high), which is not what a market counting a SEK 5bn inventory unwind into Q3 revenue and cash would look like; the Q3 cash flow (inventory release) is the test the hurbra preview names.
findings.independence: Inventory figures also in https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/; India timing from Jefferies in https://www.placera.se/telegram/ericsson-ericsson-faller-efter-rapport-som-inte-levde-upp-till-forvantningar-analytikerkommentarer-20260714. Vodafone Idea says its network investment will 'intensify in coming quarters' with orders already placed with Ericsson, Nokia and Samsung (https://www.communicationstoday.co.in/vodafone-idea-enters-execution-phase-in-fy27/). Partly offsets finding 1 (same Networks volume question, different evidence).

findings.finding: The Networks adj gross margin bar sits near the top of the guided 48-50% range (analyst average 49.7% at guide time; Q2 actual 50.4%) while the company itself flagged 'some pressure' from rollout mix and said component cost impact 'builds through H2'; TrendForce's July survey still had conventional DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 after ~60% in Q2, and price increases to customers are only 'gradually visible'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 adj GM beat (48.4% vs 48.1%) and Networks margin was 50.4%, yet the stock fell 7-10% on sales and the lowered Q3 margin guide; Barclays then said implied Q3 EBITA could be mid-single-digit % below market and Morgan Stanley put Networks gross profit ~2% below market (placera 2026-07-14).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had priced a margin at the low end, Infront's group EBITA consensus would have come down from July; instead it sits at SEK 7.9bn (14.2%) and Handelsbanken is at SEK 8.1bn. The memory-cost series kept rising after the guide was set, and no preview found reconciles the 49.7% expectation with it.
findings.independence: TrendForce Q3 2026 memory forecast https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260703-13134.html (2026-07-03); Ericsson's own cost warning https://www.lightreading.com/finance/ericsson-warns-of-price-rises-to-counter-high-component-costs (2026-07-14); Nokia was 'not immune' to memory costs (https://kfgo.com/2026/07/23/nokia-q2-profit-beat-on-ai-demand/). Macro-to-company transmission is a proxy; the company has only said 'some pressure', not how much. Segment is ~63% of sales; IPR (high margin) and CSS can offset at group level.

findings.finding: Danske Bank (2026-10-05) cut its target to SEK 110 from 115 and its Q3 adj EBITA estimate by 1%, saying US operators have postponed some investments to 2027 and component costs pressure margins from Q4; the Q3 report carries the Q4 outlook, where Networks' seasonal pattern is +17% QoQ, so a soft Q4 guide from a new CEO is the line most able to move the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: lowered Q3 Networks margin guide plus cost warning coincided with a 7-10% fall. Q3 2025: a positive outlook alongside a beat produced a ~20% ADR rally. Guide direction has decided the sign on the last prints.
findings.why_not_priced: One broker's channel read, published nine days ago; the consensus Infront compiled three days later still has Q3 EBITA at SEK 7.9bn and nothing visible in the bar reflects a weaker Q4. If deferrals were priced, the stock's 5-day tape would not be up 1.7% into the print.
findings.independence: Verizon cut 2026 capex to $16.0-16.5bn from ~$17bn with wireless the cut line (https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/verizon-earnings-slashing-capital-spending-acknowledges-network-leadership-is-past, early 2026, already public). Dell'Oro still forecasts flat 2026 RAN (https://www.telecomtv.com/content/the-future-of-ran/ran-market-stabilises-at-35bn-omdia-54878/amp/). Same placera document as finding 5 (Handelsbanken, opposite sign).

findings.finding: Handelsbanken (2026-10-05) reiterated Buy, raised its target to SEK 129 from 125 and estimates Q3 adj EBITA at SEK 8.1bn, above the SEK 7.9bn Infront consensus, citing easy North America comparisons from a weak Q3 2025 and expecting stable gross-margin guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITA beats alone have not paid: Q2 2026 adj EBITA beat by ~1.5-3% and the stock fell 7-10% (placera 2026-07-14).
findings.why_not_priced: A single bank's estimate 2.5% above consensus; the stock is still 24% below that bank's SEK 129 target, so the market is not trading on it.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 adj EBITA ex the SEK 7.6bn iconectiv gain was ~SEK 8.2bn (hurbra, https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/), which makes 8.1bn a flat-YoY ask. Shares the placera document with finding 4.

findings.finding: This is Per Narvinger's first report as CEO (took over 2026-10-01, internal Networks chief since 1997, read as continuity); restructuring for 2026 is guided 'elevated' with FY consensus SEK -5.5bn and much incurred in H1, leaving room for a new-CEO charge or new targets below the adjusted line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 booked new Swedish restructuring and the ADR fell 5.4%, but on sales and North America, not on the charge. Restructuring sits outside adjusted EBITA, which is what the bar is set on.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition is known; the size of any first-report reset is not. No preview found quantifies it, which is why it is filed small.
findings.independence: Restructuring guide and FY consensus from Ericsson's data-points page https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points; David Hammarwall (ex-T-Mobile unit head) now runs Networks from 2026-10-01 (https://mfn.se/all/a/ericsson/ericsson-appoints-david-hammarwall-head-of-business-area-networks-a3d2e0f9).

findings.finding: The SEK 15bn buyback (2026-04-23 to 2027-03-31) had taken treasury stock from 38.0m to 105.7m B shares by 2026-09-04, ~67.7m shares or ~2% of shares outstanding in about four months, and Ericsson stepped up purchases after the July fall; the report is where the pace and any extension are disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 returned SEK 8.2bn including SEK 3.2bn buybacks and the stock still fell 7-10%; capital return has not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Known programme; the only unpriced part is a possible acceleration or extension, at net cash of SEK 59.8bn (Q2). Small by construction.
findings.independence: The buyback step-up after the July drop is listed on efn.se's Ericsson page (https://efn.se/bors/instrument/17921/eric_b/oversikt); same Ericsson data-points document as findings 1 and 9.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed-out: the ADR is 29.95% below its 52-week high and 5.19% above its low after two consecutive negative print reactions, with 74.8m ADR shares short at 10.2 days to cover and a call-heavy put/call OI ratio of 0.31, so an in-line or better print has a short-cover mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, after a weak run into the print, the ADR rallied ~20.6% intraday on a beat with a better North America (fool.com 2025-10-14).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public; what is not in the price is the asymmetry it creates. Days to cover is measured on the thin ADR line and part of the short is likely arbitrage against Stockholm, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Tape from the sealed baseline (spot 9.625, -29.95% from high, +5.19% from low); 52-week high SEK 128.45 on 2026-06-03 per Dow Jones via https://www.itiger.com/news/2654404166.

findings.finding: Ericsson signed IPR licences in July 2026 with a top-10 smartphone vendor (Transsion per the hurbra preview) and a payment-terminal vendor, lifting annualized recurring IPR revenue to ~SEK 13.5bn; new licences signed in-quarter can carry catch-up payments for past periods, which would land in Q3 sales and EBITA at near-100% margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IPR was the line that made Q2 organic sales -1% (prior-year partial settlement); the stock fell 7-10% that day, so this line has moved the headline.
findings.why_not_priced: The recurring run-rate is published; a catch-up amount is not, and Q2 IPR was already SEK 3.4bn (~13.5bn annualized), so the consensus may hold IPR flat. If catch-up were modelled, the group revenue consensus (55.4bn) would sit above the segment sum it matches.
findings.independence: Q2 IPR SEK 3.4bn and the Transsion licence from https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/. The catch-up mechanism is inference; the company has not said one exists.

baseline_tension: Skew is unavailable (null) and put/call OI is call-heavy at 0.31; the 20-day run-up is -4% and the stock sits near its 52-week low, so my slight negative lean runs mildly against a washed-out setup, which is why p_up is held at 48 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning): 10.2 days to cover on the ADR short is a reason to shrink negatives; Networks GM finding -1.2 -> -1.0 and Q4 guide/deferral finding -1.0 -> -0.9.
Rule 2 (one-offs): new-CEO restructuring sits below adjusted EBITA, the line the bar is set on; -0.3 -> -0.2.
